title: Before publishing v0.6.2: state the missing provenance attestation in the release notes
description:
Filed at the orchestrator's explicit ruling (2026-09-14), after QCLI-271's own notes recorded this decision twice (notes 26, 28) and it still never reached a place the actual publisher would see it -- a closed task's implementationNotes is not a surface anyone reads before running a command. The orchestrator's framing: "The person who needs these two lines is whoever writes the GitHub Release at publish time, and nothing currently will."

Background: quest-cli's CI/OIDC publish path is dead (GitHub's org-wide immutable-subject-claim policy vs. npm Trusted Publishing -- see QCLI-271/QCLI-210 for the full, hedged epistemic history). The user already decided to publish 0.6.2 MANUALLY (classic npm login + OTP, not OIDC), accepting the consequence below. This task exists only to make sure that consequence is stated where a publisher -- possibly a future session, possibly the user themself -- will actually read it: the GitHub Release description and/or CHANGELOG.md, at or immediately after the moment of publish. docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md's publish step (step 7, dispatching release.yml) is a reasonable insertion point for a pointer to this task.

Carry both lines verbatim (not paraphrased) into wherever the release is announced:

(a) "0.6.2 ships without a provenance attestation, because provenance requires the CI OIDC path, which is currently dead."

(b) "versions published before 2026-09-10 carry permanently dangling provenance links (the repository recreation destroyed the commits/build runs they point to) and cannot be repaired -- npm forbids republishing a version."

Line (a) especially must appear wherever the release is announced, so a consumer who checks the packument for a provenance attestation and finds none reads it as an expected, already-explained gap -- not as tampering.

This does not gate the v0.6.2 tag (already created and verified) or block the manual publish itself -- npm publish remains the user's own direct call, never an orchestrator's or a session's initiative.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Line (a) ("0.6.2 ships without a provenance attestation, because provenance requires the CI OIDC path, which is currently dead.") appears verbatim in the v0.6.2 GitHub Release description and/or CHANGELOG.md
Line (b) (the pre-2026-09-10 permanently dangling gitHeads explanation) appears verbatim in the same place
Whoever publishes v0.6.2 encountered this content before or at the moment of publish, not after -- state where it was placed and why that placement reaches a publisher

finalSummary: Both lines landed in CHANGELOG.md's 0.6.2 section under a new "Known limitations" heading, carried near-verbatim and bolded (AC1, AC2 checked -- diff-verified). AC3 is honestly NOT met and stays unchecked: v0.6.2 was actually published tonight (manually, via the token-based path in QCLI-285) BEFORE this CHANGELOG fix landed, not after or during it as the AC required -- the publish happened, then the CHANGELOG gap was found (by the orchestrator, cross-checked against CHANGELOG.md directly) and fixed as a follow-up commit. The tag does not move to accommodate this (established ruling: the tag names the qualified binaries, not the changelog prose), so there is no way to retroactively make AC3 true for this specific release. Filed QCLI-286 to address the actual mechanism that let this happen (a CHANGELOG section rolled forward from a failed 0.6.1 release absorbed five later fixes invisibly) so it does not recur on the next release, which is the more valuable fix than perfecting this one instance.
